pr_title: opt: duplicate all table metadata fields when duplicating a scan
pr_body:
This commit fixes incorrect duplication of `TableMeta` when duplicating
scans, such as in the `SplitDisjuction` exploration rule. Previously,
`ScalarExpr`s in the table metadata were not being duplicated when the
table metadata was duplicated. This resulted in panics when trying to
access these fields.

All the fields of `TableMeta` are now duplicated correctly. Column IDs
in `ScalarExpr` fields are remapped to the newly generated column IDs.

This commit also simplifies the explanation for when column IDs can be
reused.

Fixes #52207

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/52499)

issue_context.title: opt: copy TableMeta.PartialIndexPredicates in Metadata.AddTable to avoid panics
issue_context.body:
The `SplitDisjunction` and `SplitDisjunctionAddKey` rules duplicate their input `ScanPrivate`s in order to create a new Scan that will be `UNION`ed with the original. In order to safely duplicate the `ScanPrivate`, [a new `TableMeta` is created with new column IDs](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/5011a06a25b0845ff9ebbff8e49e3aabe6da9c0d/pkg/sql/opt/xform/custom_funcs.go#L3051-L3053).

This creates problems with the current partial index implementation. For `SELECT` queries, partial index predicate expressions are built by optbuilder with the scope of the canonical scan, and stored on the table metadata. The first issue here is that duplicating table metadata with `Metadata.AddTable` does not copy the parsed predicate expressions to the new `TableMeta`. However, even if the predicate expressions were copied, they would not be scoped correctly to the new table and column IDs.

A critical problem I see is that we need a way to re-build predicate expressions when tables are duplicated, but there's no precedent or ability, as far as I know, to invoke the optbuilder during transformation.

To reproduce the problem:

```
exec-ddl
CREATE TABLE a (
  k INT PRIMARY KEY,
  i INT,
  s STRING,
  t STRING,
  INDEX idx_s (s),
  INDEX idx_i_200_to_250 (i) WHERE i > 200 AND i < 250
)
----

opt
SELECT * FROM a WHERE (i > 215 AND i < 230) OR s = 'baz'
----
```

review_comments: I like that it turns out we already had the callback function basically written. Nice that you noticed this.
Ya it was a great feeling when I realized in `DuplicateScanPrivate` that we just needed to pass `c.RemapCols` as the callback.
